4.subject: A small brass cyclotron device, one solid brass chamber about ten centimetres across with exactly two round flat magnet poles, top and bottom, edges sharp and unmoving, beside a gold medal lying flat on dark forest green cloth.
4.action: Both objects rest motionless on the cloth; the medal catches the lamplight and holds a steady warm gleam.
4.environment: A 1930s laboratory desk at night: dark walnut surface, a green-shaded desk lamp at frame left as the single warm light source, darkness behind with nothing identifiable.
4.camera: Medium shot, 85mm compression lens, slightly low angle so the device and medal sit with quiet dignity.
4.lighting: Single warm green-shaded desk lamp from frame left, amber glow, the medal reflecting a soft gold highlight, shadows falling gently right into darkness.
4.composition: Vertical 9:16 frame, a quiet still life: two objects on cloth on a desk, device and medal side by side in the middle third, the medal slightly lower and right of the device, green cloth pooling beneath them, empty dark desk above, nothing else in the room visible.
4.motion: A small brass cyclotron device, one solid brass chamber with two round flat magnet poles, top and bottom, beside a gold medal lying flat on dark forest green cloth, both motionless on the cloth. The device edges stay sharp and unmoving; the medal holds a steady warm gleam; nothing warps, multiplies or melts. 4.ending_frame: The frame widened just enough to hold both objects with space around them, the medal still gleaming, the device edges still sharp.

5.subject: The same cream paper napkin from scene two, lying flat and centred on the dark walnut library table, its spiral drawn as a plain pencil sketch: thin grey graphite lines, hand-drawn, slightly uneven, clearly drawn on paper.

bible.world: The University of California Berkeley campus: a high-ceilinged library reading room with tall windows and long oak tables, and a small cluttered physics laboratory with a wooden desk, brass instruments and a chalkboard. One coherent campus, one coherent decade.
bible.palette: Warm amber lamplight, aged brass, dark walnut wood, cream paper, deep forest green cloth, muted slate blue dusk sky in the final shot only. No bright primaries anywhere.
bible.lighting: One dominant warm source per scene: a desk lamp or low sun through tall windows, falling from the left, with soft shadows and gentle falloff into darkness. The same warm lamp glow unifies scenes one to four; scene five cools to dusk blue outside while the lamp stays warm inside.
bible.weather: None indoors; the only exterior is the final dusk aerial, clear and calm with a still sky.
bible.season: Early autumn, mild California weather: soft daylight through glass, no rain, no snow.
continuity_rules: The cyclotron device is identical in every shot: a small brass chamber about ten centimetres across, two round flat magnet poles top and bottom, sitting on the same dark walnut desk.
The same wooden desk, same green desk lamp with a warm bulb, and same amber light direction appear in scenes one, three and four.
The napkin is the same cream paper napkin with the same pencil spiral sketch in scenes two and five.
The man in scene two is seen only from behind: dark 1920s suit, short dark hair, so no face ever needs to match.
Time of day is consistent: warm interior lamplight throughout, dusk only in the final aerial.
The gold Nobel medal in scene four lies on the same dark forest green cloth beside the same device.
